CHIEF COMPLAINT
Right index finger pain from skiing injury.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Ms. James is a 42-year-old female presenting with right index finger pain sustained during a skiing accident this past Saturday, approximately 5 days ago. Patient reports she was skiing double black diamond slopes when she lost control, flipped down the slope, and jammed her index finger on an object. She denies other injuries from the fall. Pain is rated 7 out of 10. Patient has taken ibuprofen without significant relief. She has not applied ice or worn a splint prior to this visit.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Negative for other injuries or systemic complaints.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Chronic constipation. History of appendectomy at age 7.

MEDICATIONS
Miralax for chronic constipation.

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient is an active skier.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Right index finger examination reveals tenderness to palpation, pain with traction, and pain with squeezing over the distal interphalangeal (DIP) joint and proximal interphalangeal (PIP) joint. X-ray of right hand shows normal alignment of all joints and bones with no fractures identified.

RESULTS
X-ray of right hand: Normal, no fractures.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Sprain of the distal interphalangeal (DIP) joint of the right index finger. Patient to be fitted with splint for right index finger. Prescribed Mobic 15 mg once daily, quantity 14 tablets for anti-inflammatory treatment. Follow-up appointment in 2 weeks to assess healing and determine need for hand therapy.
